title: Lo, la, le
goal: Stop repeating nouns: use direct and indirect object pronouns, alone and together.

lessons.title: It and them
lessons.notes:
A **direct object** is the thing the verb acts on: I buy **the shirt**. To avoid repeating it, Spanish uses **lo, la, los, las**, matching the noun's gender and number:
**¿Compras la camisa? - Sí, la compro.** (Yes, I'm buying it.)
**¿Tienes los boletos? - No, no los tengo.**
The pronoun goes **before** the conjugated verb (and after **no**). English puts "it" after the verb; Spanish puts it in front.
**lo** also means "it" for an idea: **No lo sé.** (I don't know.) **Lo siento.** (I'm sorry - literally "I feel it".)
They work for people too: **lo veo** = I see him; **la conozco** = I know her.

sentences.es: ¿La camisa azul? Sí, la compro.
sentences.en: The blue shirt? Yes, I'll buy it.
accept_en: The blue shirt? Yes, I'm buying it.
The blue shirt? Yes, I'll take it.

sentences.es: Me gusta este suéter. Lo compro.
sentences.en: I like this jumper. I'll buy it.
accept_en: I like this sweater. I'll take it.
I like this jumper. I'll take it.

sentences.es: ¿Tienes los boletos? - No, no los tengo.
sentences.en: Do you have the tickets? - No, I don't have them.
accept_en: Have you got the tickets? - No, I haven't got them.

sentences.es: No encuentro mis gafas. ¿Las ves?
sentences.en: I can't find my glasses. Can you see them?
accept_en: I can't find my glasses. Do you see them?

sentences.es: ¿Dónde está el museo? - No lo sé.
sentences.en: Where is the museum? - I don't know.
accept_en: Where's the museum? - I don't know.

sentences.es: ¿Conoces a Marta? - Sí, la conozco.
sentences.en: Do you know Marta? - Yes, I know her.

sentences.es: Veo a Carlos todos los días. Lo veo en el trabajo.
sentences.en: I see Carlos every day. I see him at work.

sentences.es: ¿Encontraste las llaves? - Sí, las encontré.
sentences.en: Did you find the keys? - Yes, I found them.

sentences.es: El pollo, lo cocino en el horno.
sentences.en: The chicken, I make it in the oven.
accept_en: I make the chicken in the oven.
I cook the chicken in the oven.

lessons.title: Me, you, us
lessons.notes:
For people in conversation the object pronouns are the ones you know from reflexive verbs:
**me** (me) · **te** (you) · **nos** (us)
**Mi mamá me llama todos los días.** = My mum calls me every day.
**¿Te ayudo?** = Shall I help you?
**Nos invitaron a la fiesta.** = They invited us to the party.
Same position: before the conjugated verb.
Useful verbs that take a person as object: **ayudar** (to help), **invitar** (to invite), **esperar** (to wait for - no "for" needed in Spanish), **llevar** (to take someone somewhere).
**¿Me esperas?** = Will you wait for me?

items.note: Te invito = I invite you, and also: it's my treat.

sentences.es: Mi mamá me llama todos los domingos.
sentences.en: My mum calls me every Sunday.
accept_en: My mom calls me every Sunday.
My mother rings me every Sunday.

lessons.title: To him, to them: le, les
lessons.notes:
An **indirect object** is the person who **receives**: I give the book **to Ana**. Spanish uses:
**me** · **te** · **le** (to him / her / you-usted) · **nos** · **les** (to them / you-ustedes)
Verbs of giving and telling take them: **dar** (to give), **decir**, **escribir**, **mandar** (to send), **regalar** (to give as a present), **preguntar** (to ask).
**Le doy el regalo.** = I give him / her the present.
Spanish often says the person too, with **a**, even though **le** is there: **Le escribí a mi abuela.** It sounds natural, and it makes clear who **le** is.
**dar** is irregular in yo: **doy**, and in the preterite: **di, diste, dio, dimos, dieron**.

items.note: doy, das, da... Preterite: di, dio.
To ask a question. To ask for something: pedir.

sentences.es: Le doy el regalo a mi hermana.
sentences.en: I give the present to my sister.
accept_en: I give my sister the present.
I'm giving my sister the present.
I give the gift to my sister.

sentences.es: Le escribí un mensaje a mi abuela.
sentences.en: I wrote my grandmother a message.
accept_en: I wrote a message to my grandmother.
I sent my grandma a message.

sentences.es: ¿Les mandaste las fotos a tus padres?
sentences.en: Did you send the photos to your parents?
accept_en: Did you send your parents the photos?

sentences.es: Para su cumpleaños le regalé un libro.
sentences.en: For his birthday I gave him a book.
accept_en: For her birthday I gave her a book.
I gave him a book for his birthday.

sentences.es: Voy a preguntarle al profesor.
sentences.en: I'm going to ask the teacher.

sentences.es: ¿Me prestas tu bicicleta?
sentences.en: Will you lend me your bike?
accept_en: Can you lend me your bicycle?

sentences.es: El médico les dio pastillas.
sentences.en: The doctor gave them tablets.

sentences.es: Mis amigos me dieron una torta.
sentences.en: My friends gave me a cake.

sentences.es: ¿Qué le dijiste a Pedro?
sentences.en: What did you say to Pedro?

lessons.title: Two pronouns: se lo
lessons.notes:
When you use both, the **person comes first**, the thing second: **me lo**, **te la**, **nos los**.
**¿Me das el libro? - Sí, te lo doy.** (Yes, I'll give it to you.)
One trap: **le** or **les** before **lo / la / los / las** becomes **se** ("le lo" is too hard to say):
**Le doy el regalo.** -> **Se lo doy.** (I give it to him / her.)
With an infinitive or **-ando** form, the pronouns can also go on the end, as one word (add an accent to keep the stress):
**Te lo voy a dar.** = **Voy a dártelo.**
**Estoy comprándola.** = **La estoy comprando.**

accept_en: will you give it to me

items.en: I give it to him / her

sentences.es: ¿Me das la sal? - Sí, te la doy.
sentences.en: Will you pass me the salt? - Yes, here you are.
accept_en: Can you give me the salt? - Yes, I'll give it to you.
Will you give me the salt? - Yes, I'll give it to you.

sentences.es: Es mi libro. ¿Me lo das?
sentences.en: It's my book. Will you give it to me?
accept_en: It's my book. Can you give it to me?

sentences.es: El regalo para Ana: se lo doy mañana.
sentences.en: The present for Ana: I'll give it to her tomorrow.
accept_en: Ana's present: I'll give it to her tomorrow.

sentences.es: Carlos no sabía la noticia, entonces se la dije.
sentences.en: Carlos didn't know the news, so I told him.
accept_en: Carlos didn't know the news, so I told it to him.

sentences.es: Me gusta ese abrigo. Voy a comprarlo.
sentences.en: I like that coat. I'm going to buy it.
accept: Me gusta ese abrigo. Lo voy a comprar.

sentences.es: No entiendo. ¿Me lo explicas otra vez?
sentences.en: I don't understand. Will you explain it to me again?
accept_en: I don't understand. Can you explain it to me again?

sentences.es: Te voy a mostrar las fotos del viaje.
sentences.en: I'm going to show you the photos from the trip.
accept: Voy a mostrarte las fotos del viaje.
accept_en: I'll show you the photos from the trip.
I'm going to show you the trip photos.

sentences.es: Es un secreto. No se lo dije a nadie.
sentences.en: It's a secret. I didn't tell anyone.
accept_en: It's a secret. I didn't tell anybody.
It's a secret. I told nobody.

sentences.es: ¿Las fotos? Se las mandé a mis padres.
sentences.en: The photos? I sent them to my parents.
